description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 30% to 55%. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 29% and increasing slightly to about 32% over the range. The "MEND" method, shown as a brown line with diamond markers, begins near 36%, rises to about 44% at 10², and then levels off near 45% at 10³. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at roughly 32% and increases steadily to approximately 38%. The "MEMIT" method, indicated by a purple line with star markers, begins near 35%, peaks at about 46% at 10², and then slightly decreases to around 45% at 10³. The "IKE" method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at about 31% and increases to approximately 41% at 10³. The "ROME" method, represented by a green line with square markers, begins at about 43% and rises sharply to approximately 57% at 10³.
